 Retail Target posts best sales growth in five years, raises guidance
 Published Wed, Nov 18 2026 12:01 AM EST Updated 22 Min Ago Laya Neelakandan @in/layaneelakandan @Laya_neel WATCH LIVE Key Points Target beat third-quarter sales expectations and raised its guidance as it continues a turnaround effort.
 The retailer is undergoing a turnaround under CEO Michael Fiddelke.
 Target said changes to its stores and assortment are resonating with shoppers.
 In this article
 TGT 
 Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Shoppers walk past the entrance to a Target store in Washington, Aug. 4, 2026. Kevin Carter | Getty Images Target on Wednesday reported its best sales growth in over five years and beat Wall Street's revenue expectations, the latest signs of its turnaround strategy taking hold.
 The retailer said its net sales grew 7.1% during the quarter. Comparable sales rose 5.6%, compared to StreetAccount estimates of up 3.8%. That growth was boosted by a 5% increase in comparable traffic, Target added. 
 "[It's] a healthy sign that guests are responding to our changes and choosing Target more often," CEO Michael Fiddelke told reporters. 
 Digital comparable sales jumped nearly 10% during the quarter.
 Encouraged by the growth, Target raised its full-year guidance, upping its net sales growth guidance by 1 percentage point to around 6%. It's also expecting full-year operating income margin rate to be around 6.2%, which includes roughly 1.1 percentage points of benefit from tariff refunds.
 The company also said it's now expecting full-year earnings per share to be in a range of $10.65 to $11.40, compared with prior guidance of between $9.90 and $10.90. 
 "The changes we've made across our assortment and guest experience are adding up," Fiddelke told reporters. "While we're encouraged by the progress, we know there's more work ahead to sustain this momentum and deliver consistent growth over time."
 Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
 Earnings per share: $2.65, it was not immediately clear if it compared to the $2.07 expected
 Revenue: $27.07 billion vs. $26.56 billion expected
 For the quarter ended Oct. 31, Target reported net income of $1.21 billion, or $2.65 per share, up from $689 million, or $1.51 per share, the year prior. 
 This year, the company said it's invested approximately $3.8 billion in capital expenditures, up nearly $1 billion from last year. Because of those returns, Fiddelke said Target is now expecting to invest between $5 billion and $6 billion in capex next year. 
 The company said it saw particular strength in beauty, which saw 9% growth, and food and beverage, where sales grew nearly 7%. The retailer added that net sales rose in all three months of the third quarter, with the strongest performance during the back-to-school season. 
 Fiddelke told reporters the quarter's strength showed "continued progress" toward Target's priorities that it outlined at the beginning of its turnaround. 
 As it looks to the holiday season, Target said it's marketing thousands of products priced at $5 and under, along with new AI-powered shopping experiences to drive engagement. Fiddelke said Target is "encouraged" by shopping behaviors it's seen so far in the current quarter.
 The big-box retailer has been showing signs of returning to growth, as it sees stronger sales trends after years of flat revenue. The strong sales trends come after Target last quarter hiked its full fiscal-year outlook and said it saw "broad-based" strength across its various categories.
 It's also lowered prices on more than 10,000 items in an effort to get customers back into its stores, especially as consumer sentiment lags and inflation remains high. The retailer said on Wednesday that it cut prices on an additional roughly 2,000 items during the third quarter.
 Target's stock is up more than 60% this year.
